topicLabel: Whether Solace should replace charging cases after reports of overnight battery drain
title: Solace opens a review of hearing-aid cases that drain overnight
body: Solace Audio is reviewing reports that charging cases for its S3 hearing aids lose most of their charge overnight even when the devices are stored inside. The company says it has received a small number of complaints and is testing returned cases from two production runs. Users who depend on the aids while traveling want replacement cases immediately; Solace says it will first identify whether the drain comes from the case or a paired device. No safety issue has been reported. The review concerns charging hardware, not the S4 model's speech-processing software.

topicLabel: Whether Solace should replace charging cases after reports of overnight battery drain
title: Solace says overnight case drain may involve user settings
body: Solace Audio says reports of overnight battery loss in S3 hearing-aid charging cases may stem from Bluetooth settings that keep devices connected after storage. The company is checking cases but does not support replacing every unit before it can reproduce the problem. Hearing specialists say users should not be asked to troubleshoot a device they rely on every day. Solace has offered a support line and requested case serial numbers. The discussion is about the S3 charging case, distinct from software choices on the newer S4 hearing aid.

topicLabel: Whether Solace should replace charging cases after reports of overnight battery drain
title: Clinics ask Solace for a simple remedy to S3 case failures
body: A group of hearing clinics wants Solace to offer replacement charging cases to S3 owners who experience overnight drain. Clinicians say patients often discover the problem only when they need their devices the next morning, and repeated diagnostic visits can be difficult for people with limited mobility. The manufacturer is testing returned cases and says it will announce a remedy after comparing hardware batches. Some retailers support a broader exchange, while others favor repair after a confirmed fault. The request is limited to S3 charging cases.

topicLabel: Whether Solace should replace charging cases after reports of overnight battery drain
title: Retailers recommend case-by-case checks for Solace S3 owners
body: Solace retailers recommend checking the charging contacts and connection settings before replacing S3 cases reported to drain overnight. They say a targeted service visit may resolve some complaints without discarding working equipment. Patient advocates respond that the company should provide a temporary loaner while checks are underway. Solace has not published a service bulletin and is still evaluating returned units. The question is how to handle the S3 case reports, not whether the newer S4's speech features should be changed.

topicLabel: Whether Solace should reduce noise filtering in its S4 speech enhancement update
title: Solace considers softer noise filtering after S4 users miss quiet voices
body: Solace Audio is collecting feedback on its S4 speech enhancement update after some users said the new noise filter suppresses quiet voices along with background sounds. The company says the feature improves conversations in busy rooms but is testing a less aggressive setting. Audiologists have asked for a slider that lets each wearer choose a balance. Solace has not changed the default and is inviting volunteers to compare sample recordings. The issue concerns signal processing in S4 software, not the S3 charging-case battery reports.

topicLabel: Whether Solace should reduce noise filtering in its S4 speech enhancement update
title: Some S4 wearers want Solace to preserve the stronger filter
body: Many Solace S4 users say the latest speech enhancement is the first setting that makes restaurant conversations manageable. They oppose weakening the noise filter across all devices because a quieter voice may still be difficult to hear amid dishes and traffic. Other wearers report that the software clips soft speech. Solace is testing alternatives and has not selected a new default. The exchange is about the S4's noise-filtering update, separate from a hardware review of S3 charging cases.

topicLabel: Whether Solace should reduce noise filtering in its S4 speech enhancement update
title: Hearing advisers urge a user control for Solace S4 filtering
body: Hearing advisers have asked Solace to add a user-adjustable noise filter to its S4 speech enhancement update. They say people vary in how they distinguish voices from background sound, so a single stronger setting will not work for every wearer. Solace says an adjustable control may require additional testing to prevent distortion. Some users prefer the current setting and want any change to remain optional. The company is reviewing software feedback from volunteers; the S4 update has no connection to battery behavior in the earlier S3 case.

topicLabel: Whether Solace should reduce noise filtering in its S4 speech enhancement update
title: Solace users warn that a quieter filter could revive crowded-room problems
body: A user group cautioned Solace against reducing the S4 noise filter after members reported clearer conversations in cafes and waiting rooms. They accept that a few quiet voices are softened but say stronger background suppression is a major improvement. Audiologists favor personal controls rather than one global adjustment. Solace has not announced a release date for any change and continues collecting comparisons. This debate concerns software behavior on the S4 hearing aid, while S3 owners are separately discussing charging-case replacement.

topicLabel: Whether the Glenford bridge should accept contactless payment at its toll booth
title: Glenford pilots contactless toll payment at the north booth
body: Glenford's bridge authority has begun a six-week trial of contactless card payments at the north toll booth. Drivers can still use coins or a prepaid tag, and attendants will record how often each method is chosen. The authority says the pilot will assess queue times and equipment reliability before any permanent installation. Cash lanes remain open on both approaches. A public report is expected later in the season, after which the board may consider adding readers at the southern entrance.

topicLabel: How Willow Park will repair the clock inside its botanical greenhouse
title: Willow Park greenhouse clock removed for restoration
body: The large clock inside Willow Park's botanical greenhouse has been removed for a mechanical restoration. Conservators found worn brass gears but no damage to the painted dial, which will remain in place while the movement is repaired. The greenhouse will stay open, though visitors may notice a temporary display explaining the work. The parks trust expects the clock to return before the spring plant exhibition. A local horologist is donating several hours of labor, and the trust will cover materials from its maintenance fund.

topicLabel: Whether Cairn should add a close-focus mode to its field binoculars
title: Cairn asks birders to evaluate a close-focus binocular prototype
body: Cairn Optics has shown birding groups a binocular prototype designed to focus on insects and plants at shorter distances. The company says the hinge has been adjusted to preserve alignment while users shift between near and distant views. Testers will report on weight, eye relief, and how easily the focus wheel can be turned with gloves. Cairn has not confirmed production plans. The prototype shares the housing of its current field model but uses a different internal lens arrangement.

topicLabel: What a coastal radar trial can reveal about low cloud near Merrow Bay
title: Merrow Bay hosts a portable radar for fog research
body: A portable weather radar has been installed near Merrow Bay to study low cloud formation along the coast. Researchers will compare its readings with lighthouse visibility logs and measurements from two inland stations. The trial runs for six weeks and does not provide public storm alerts. Scientists hope the added detail will help explain why fog forms quickly on some mornings but not others. The equipment will be removed after the campaign, and the data will be archived by the regional university.

topicLabel: Whether the Ravens should extend Coach Neri's contract after a semifinal loss
title: Ravens board considers a new deal for coach after semifinal exit
body: The Ravens board is weighing a contract extension for coach Lila Neri after the club lost its semifinal match by one point. Players say Neri rebuilt the defense and gave younger athletes consistent roles, while some supporters expected a championship run after a strong regular season. The current agreement expires in June. Neri has declined to discuss negotiations until the season review is complete. The decision concerns the coach's future after the semifinal, not the club's separate proposal to replace the training hall roof.

topicLabel: Whether the Ravens should extend Coach Neri's contract after a semifinal loss
title: Ravens members urge board to seek a new coach
body: A group of Ravens members wants the board to let Coach Lila Neri's contract expire after the team's semifinal defeat. They say the squad has been eliminated at the same stage twice and needs a different approach to close matches. Players have publicly praised Neri's development work and asked management to judge the full season. The board will meet after reviewing performance data and player feedback. No replacement search has begun. The debate is about coaching after a playoff loss, separate from maintenance at the Ravens training facility.

topicLabel: Whether the Ravens should extend Coach Neri's contract after a semifinal loss
title: Former captain says Ravens should retain Neri for another season
body: Former Ravens captain Jo Wells has urged the club to extend Lila Neri's contract for one more season, arguing that the semifinal loss should not erase steady progress among younger players. Critics say close defeats point to tactical limits that may not improve with time. The board has asked the coaching staff to submit a season report before negotiations continue. Neri remains under contract through June. The current argument concerns whether to keep the coach, not a planned renovation of the team's indoor training hall.

topicLabel: Whether the Ravens should extend Coach Neri's contract after a semifinal loss
title: Supporters say the Ravens need a fresh sideline plan
body: At a club meeting, several Ravens supporters called for a new coach after Lila Neri's team fell in the semifinal for a second consecutive year. Others said injuries and a difficult away schedule contributed to the defeat. The board has not announced an extension or a departure and will review results with players next week. Neri's current deal runs until June, leaving time for a decision. Members are discussing the coach's contract after the semifinal loss, not the team's facilities budget.

topicLabel: Whether the Ravens should replace the training hall roof before next winter
title: Ravens request funds for a new roof over the training hall
body: The Ravens have asked the city for a grant to replace the roof over their indoor training hall before winter. A facilities inspection found several leaks above the equipment room and one warped panel near the west entrance. Club officials say repairs would protect stored gear and keep youth practices on schedule. The city wants a second contractor's estimate before committing funds. Players have also discussed the future of coach Lila Neri after a semifinal loss, but the roof request is a separate building project.

topicLabel: Whether the Ravens should replace the training hall roof before next winter
title: Council asks Ravens to patch the hall roof before seeking a full rebuild
body: A city budget committee says the Ravens should patch the damaged sections of their training hall roof and return with a longer-term plan next year. Members worry that a full replacement would use funds reserved for public recreation sites. The club says temporary repairs may not survive heavy snow and could damage stored equipment if another leak opens. The inspection found no structural danger, and the hall remains in use. This debate concerns the building roof, not the separate board decision about coach Lila Neri's contract.

topicLabel: Whether the Ravens should replace the training hall roof before next winter
title: Parents back a lasting roof repair for Ravens youth sessions
body: Parents whose children train at the Ravens hall support replacing the roof before winter rather than relying on repeated patches. They say canceled indoor sessions would disrupt youth teams and that damp storage can ruin shared equipment. City officials want the club to contribute part of the cost or secure a second estimate. The grant application is still under review, and no work date has been set. The proposal is about maintenance of the training building, distinct from arguments over the team's coaching contract.

topicLabel: Whether the Ravens should replace the training hall roof before next winter
title: Ravens can manage winter with targeted roof repairs, says treasurer
body: The Ravens treasurer says targeted repairs to the training hall roof can keep the building usable through winter at a fraction of a full replacement. The club would inspect the patched areas after heavy rain and seek a larger grant next year. Parents favor a permanent fix, while city budget staff say a phased approach would leave money for other youth facilities. The hall remains open and has not been declared unsafe. The discussion concerns repair timing, not whether coach Neri should stay after the semifinal.
